articles.title: Canada Reminds International Students: You Can Work Only If Your Study Permit Says So
articles.excerpt: IRCC's fresh warning: the permission is printed on the permit itself, off-campus work is capped at 24 hours a week in session, and breaching the conditions can cost a student their status.
articles.nri_angle: Indians form one of the largest international student cohorts in Canada, and unauthorised work is among the most common ways their status is put at risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: H-1B Visas and Green Cards After the Midterms: What Indian Professionals Should Watch
articles.excerpt: The November 3 elections will not change anyone's visa status overnight. What they decide is which of three live bills — on H-1B salary thresholds, a proposed issuance pause, and a points-based green card system — gets a Congress willing to move it.
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for more than 70% of H-1B approvals and face the longest employment-based green card waits, so the bills below matter to them first.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Texas Agriculture Department Bars H-1B Employers From Its State Grants
articles.excerpt: Commissioner Sid Miller's October 28 policy cuts businesses employing H-1B workers out of Texas Department of Agriculture grants and challenges other state officials to follow.

sources.label: Texas Department of Agriculture announcement (via EIN Presswire)

articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are the largest H-1B group in Texas; employers who hire them now risk losing state agriculture grant eligibility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: In Texas's Rio Grande Valley, the Deportation Drive Is Galvanising the Midterm Vote
articles.excerpt: The Valley swung to Trump in 2024 over the border. Two years of domestic enforcement — a $180.6 million hit to the local economy, an ACLU poll showing 63 percent say ICE has gone too far, and deportations like a Progreso woman's within 36 hours of a hearing — are swinging it back days before the November 3 midterms.
articles.nri_angle: The Valley's story is the national one for immigrant communities, including Indian families in Texas: enforcement has shifted from the border to workplaces, hearings and missed court dates inside the country, and the November 3 result will shape funding and oversight of that machinery.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian National Convicted of Voting Illegally in 2024 US Presidential Election
articles.excerpt: A federal jury in Fort Worth convicted Khalwinder Singh Bhengura, a green card holder from India, of voting by an alien and falsely claiming US citizenship to register. Sentencing is set for February 11, 2027.

articles.nri_angle: For green card holders: voting in a federal election — or even registering by claiming citizenship — can mean prison, fines and removal from the US, even before naturalization is complete.

articles.excerpt: Salil Parekh told investors a majority-local US workforce insulates Infosys from the PERM suspension and H-1B pressure, even as individual green-card cases face delays.

articles.title: Proposed $70,000 OPT Fee Would Sharply Raise Cost of Student Work Permits
articles.excerpt: A Department of Homeland Security proposal would charge schools $70,000 for a first OPT recommendation and $30,000 for each later one, including STEM extensions — up from about $500 today — with public comments open through November 9.
articles.image_caption: An academic procession at the University of Washington (file photo, Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are one of the largest international cohorts in the US and heavily represented in STEM programmes, so a $70,000 OPT recommendation fee would directly reprice the F-1-to-first-job route many Indian graduates rely on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Republican Bill Would Raise H-1B Exemption Threshold to Nearly $140,000
articles.excerpt: House and Senate versions of the Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act would replace the $60,000 salary exemption for H-1B-dependent employers, frozen since 1998, with twice the national average wage index — nearly $140,000 today.
articles.image_caption: The US House of Representatives chamber, where the H-1B exemption bill sits in committee (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals receive the bulk of H-1B visas and Indian and Indian-origin IT services firms are among the employers most likely to be classed H-1B-dependent, so a higher exemption threshold would fall hardest on the hiring model many Indian professionals enter through.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australia Tightens Student Visa Rules: Five Changes Indian Students Must Know
articles.excerpt: Most onshore applications closed on 2 October 2026, repeat student visas now need an exemption, partners and children can rarely be included and can never join later — and provider transfers are restricted for 12 months until June 2027.

sources.label: Australian Department of Home Affairs — Changes to Student visa application rules (subclasses 500 & 590)
AUSCAN Immigration — Australia Student Visa Rules Oct 2026 Q&A

articles.nri_angle: India is one of Australia's largest sources of international students, so the onshore, family and transfer changes directly affect Indian families planning study, dependants and post-study pathways in Australia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: 2 Oct 2026: most temporary visa holders (Working Holiday, Training, Skills in Demand and others) must apply for a student visa from outside Australia — and be outside Australia at grant
Second student visa onshore only with an exemption: same-provider course completion (up to 12 extra months), DFAT/Defence sponsorship, PhD, school studies, higher-AQF progression, or provider default
Partner/children can be included only if an exemption applies (e.g. PhD, DFAT/Defence sponsorship, fully funded foreign government scholarship) — and only at the time of applying
Family cannot be added later as subsequent entrants — no exemptions
Provider-transfer restriction extended from 6 to 12 months for non-school students until 30 June 2027
Applications lodged before 2 Oct 2026 are assessed under the old rules
From 26 Oct 2026, biometrics (fingerprints, facial image) may be requested for new Indian student visa applications

articles.title: Supreme Court Refuses to Restore Immigration Judges' Power to Shelve Deportation Cases
articles.excerpt: A one-sentence emergency order leaves in place the Trump administration's same-day settlement with Texas that ended administrative closure, a docket tool used in hundreds of thousands of deportation cases.
articles.image_caption: The US Supreme Court building in Washington. The court declined on Tuesday to reinstate immigration judges' authority to shelve deportation cases through administrative closure.
articles.nri_angle: Administrative closure was one of the few tools keeping deportation cases dormant for Indian nationals waiting on backlogged green card processes; its loss means removal cases now proceed on the court's timetable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Plaintiffs Push for Fast Ruling in $100,000 H-1B Fee Case as Government Seeks Pause
articles.excerpt: In Global Nurse Force v. Trump, employers and workers want a California court to move to summary judgment on the $100,000 H-1B payment, while the administration asks to freeze the case until the Ninth Circuit rules on its appeal.
articles.image_caption: The Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building in Oakland, home to the Oakland division of the US District Court for the Northern District of California. Plaintiffs challenging the $100,000 H-1B fee have asked the court for a fast final ruling.
articles.nri_angle: The $100,000 fee fight decides whether Indian professionals and their US employers face a six-figure charge on new H-1B petitions once the current court injunctions run their course.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.nri_angle: Fewer registrations from the big IT sponsors means fewer US onsite pathways for Indian engineers; higher-wage roles now carry better lottery odds.

articles.title: Canada Extends Work Permit Measures for Haitians and Sudanese to December 2027
articles.excerpt: IRCC extended the temporary measures on the day they were set to expire, allowing eligible Haitian and Sudanese work permit holders in Canada to apply for extensions until December 30, 2027, with standard processing fees applying.
articles.nri_angle: The extension shows how Canada uses temporary public-policy measures to keep workers in status, a mechanism Indian temporary residents in Canada also rely on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: H-1B Workers Taking Microsoft Buyout Face 60-Day Deadline to Stay
articles.excerpt: Microsoft has not said whether H-1B holders are eligible for its voluntary exit offer to 60,000 employees. For visa workers who do accept and leave on December 31, USCIS rules give up to 60 days to find a new sponsor, change status, or depart.
articles.image_caption: A Microsoft sign stands outside a company office building. Microsoft's voluntary exit offer to about 60,000 employees has raised urgent questions for H-1B workers weighing whether to accept.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian H-1B workers at Microsoft in the United States, accepting a voluntary exit ends the employment behind their status and starts a 60-day window to find a new sponsor, change status, or leave.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Midterms on November 3 Will Shape H-1B, Green Card Debate
articles.excerpt: Control of Congress will decide whether H-1B and green card bills can move, while the $100,000 fee and PERM suspensions already in force rest with the executive branch
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders and green card applicants are the largest group affected by US skilled immigration policy, and the November 3 result decides whether Congress can change the caps and fees behind their waits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: White House Clears Labor Department Plan to Overhaul PERM Green Card Rules
articles.excerpt: The proposed PERM modernization (RIN 1205-AC29) cleared OIRA review on October 23 and heads to the Federal Register, with recruitment standards, layoff rules and nondiscrimination requirements in scope.
articles.image_caption: The White House in Washington, DC. The administration completed its review of the Labor Department's proposed PERM overhaul on October 23, clearing the proposal for publication in the Federal Register.
articles.nri_angle: PERM is the first step for most EB-2 and EB-3 green cards, where Indian applicants are the largest group; the overhaul's recruitment and layoff rules will shape their filings once finalized.

articles.title: Indian H-1B Worker Arrested in Ohio on Federal Child Pornography Charges
articles.excerpt: Vimalesh Prem Kumar, 39, of Blue Ash appeared in federal court on October 21 after cyber tips led agents to his accounts, prosecutors say. The complaint is an allegation, and he is presumed innocent.
articles.image_caption: Downtown Blue Ash, Ohio , USA, at the intersection of Hunt and Kenwood. Vimalesh Prem Kumar, 39, of Blue Ash, Ohio, an Indian national in the United States on an H-1B work visa, was arrested by federal agents and appeared in federal court on October 21.

articles.title: US Appeals Court Denies Constitutional Bond Hearings for Detained Migrants
articles.excerpt: The 5th Circuit ruled 10-7 that the Fifth Amendment does not require bond hearings for detained immigrants, reversing a July ruling and affecting Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi.
articles.image_caption: The ceiling of the John Minor Wisdom U.S. Court of Appeals Building in New Orleans, home of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.
articles.nri_angle: Detained migrants in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi, including long-term residents, lose a constitutional route to bond hearings; families there should pursue statutory and immigration-court options promptly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BIA Rules Returned Hearing Notice No Longer Blocks Removal Order
articles.excerpt: In Matter of Chamorro Castillo, decided October 22, the Board held that a notice mailed to the only address on file can support an in absentia removal order even when it comes back undeliverable.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Department of Justice headquarters in Washington (file photo). The Board of Immigration Appeals sits within the department's Executive Office for Immigration Review.

articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals, the largest H-1B group, gain a reopened path for overseas hires as USCIS resumes approving petitions without the $100,000 fee, though appeals could revive it.

articles.title: Palmer Luckey Calls H-1B Lobby Defense a Sham, Defenders Push Back
articles.excerpt: The Anduril founder says lobbyists defend a program widely used to undercut American wages and that silent executives know it. H-1B supporters, from Paul Graham to university leaders, say the alternative to a global hire is often a job exported abroad.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals hold the largest share of H-1B visas, so Luckey's employer-side attack on the program's lobbying defense — and defenders' warning that restrictions export jobs to cities including Bangalore — directly frames the debate affecting Indian tech workers.

articles.nri_angle: Florida's pause blocks new H-1B hires at its 12 public universities until January 5, 2027, directly affecting Indian faculty, researchers, physicians and graduates seeking campus jobs there, while existing holders and renewals are unaffected.
